tool.name: 3DTrees: SmartTile
tool.description: Tile, merge and remap point clouds

param.name: resolution_1_cm
param.label: Resolution of the high-resolution tiles (cm)
param.help: Resolution of the high-resolution tiles from the tile task, 1–100 cm (typically 1 cm). It sets the matching radius, the 3D voxel diagonal (17.32 mm at 1 cm).

param.name: mode
param.label: Prod-merged resolution
param.help: Subsampled keeps one original point per voxel; full resolution keeps every input point in record order (for example as input to ForestStructure).

param.name: merged_resolution_cm
param.label: Prod-merged resolution (cm)
param.help: Target spacing for prod-merged outputs, 1–100 cm.

param.label: Add OriginalPointIndex
param.help: Numbers every point by its record position across the input files (sorted by name), as the first ExtraByte. ForestStructure uses it to restore the source order after COPC and reproduce Julia's results.

param.label: Prod-merged formats
param.help: Select one or more output encodings for prod-merged products.

param.name: input_files
param.label: Input LAZ/LAS files
param.help: One or more source point clouds to tile and subsample.

param.label: Tile length (m)
param.help: Target tile edge length in meters.

param.label: Tile buffer (m)
param.help: Overlap added around each tile in meters. The tile grid always starts at the south-west corner of the data extent.

param.label: Tiling threshold (MB)
param.help: Skip tiling for a single input below this size and still create normalized subsampled outputs.

param.label: Subsampling method
param.help: Point kept for each voxel: center of mass is the mean of the original points in the voxel; nearest to centroid is the original point closest to that mean.

repeat.name: tile_outputs
repeat.title: Subsampled output
repeat.help: One collection per entry, in this order (first entry = subsampled output 1). Each resolution may appear only once. All resolutions come from one read of the inputs. Typically a low resolution (10 cm) for the segmentation models and a high resolution (1 cm) as merge geometry.

param.name: resolution_cm
param.label: Resolution (cm)
param.help: Voxel size, 1–100 cm. Every resolution is computed from the original points.

param.name: format
param.label: Format
param.help: COPC LAZ only for viewers or spatial reads; SmartTile merge accepts LAZ and COPC LAZ. PLY is binary XYZ with the CRS as a comment line.

param.name: type
param.label: Model
param.help: The model that produced the segmented files.
param.option: SegmentAnyTree, ForestMamba or other point predictions

param.label: Instance dimension
param.help: Name of the prediction instance dimension in the segmented files, for example PredInstance_SAT or PredInstance_FM.

validator.message: Use letters, numbers, and underscores only; start with a letter or underscore.

param.name: input_tree_files
param.label: Tree tables from 3dtrees_raycloudtools
param.help: Both the *_trees.txt and *_trees_info.txt table for every segmented tile; required to keep whole trees and their tree IDs.

param.name: input_tree_meshes
param.label: QSM tree meshes from 3dtrees_raycloudtools
param.help: Optional: the *_trees_mesh.ply of every segmented tile (RayCloudTools 1.3.0 or newer, with per-face tree IDs). Filtered with the same IDs as the tiles and tables.

param.name: input_segmented
param.label: Primary segmented files
param.help: Segmented prediction files, in the same tile layout as the high-resolution tiles.

param.name: input_res1
param.label: High-resolution tiles
param.help: The high-resolution subsampled tiles from the tile task (typically 1 cm): merge transfers the predictions onto them.

param.name: input_original_laz
param.label: Original LAZ/LAS files
param.help: Original uploaded files to enrich with predictions and use for prod-merged outputs.

param.name: tile_bounds_json
param.label: Tile bounds JSON
param.help: Tile bounds JSON emitted by the tile task for the same tiling run.

param.name: prediction_transfer_cm
param.label: Prediction transfer radius (cm)
param.help: Every high-resolution point takes the predictions of the nearest segmented point within this 3D distance, and every point must find one. The default, 17.32 cm, is the voxel diagonal of 10 cm segmentation tiles; for coarser segmentation tiles use 1.732 × their resolution (for example 34.64 cm at 20 cm).

param.label: Ownership anchor
param.help: Point of each instance whose XY position decides which tile core owns it; the centroid is the XY centroid.

param.name: enabled
param.label: Cross-tile instance reconciliation
param.help: Give retained instances that continue across a tile boundary one shared ID. Not used with RayCloudTools tree tables (whole trees keep their tile-local identity).

param.label: Overlap threshold
param.help: Minimum shared-point ratio for reconciling instances across tiles, above 0 and at most 1.

validator.message: The overlap threshold must be above 0 and at most 1.

param.name: enabled
param.label: Small cluster reassignment
param.help: After deduplication, give small instances the ID of the remaining instance with the nearest XY centroid (horizontal distance, within 5 m). Not available for RayCloudTools.

param.label: Max bounding-box volume (m3)
param.help: Instances below this axis-aligned bounding-box volume are small.

param.label: Max cluster size (points)
param.help: Only instances with fewer points on the high-resolution tiles are checked against the volume limit.

param.name: merged_file
param.label: Merged LAZ/COPC LAZ file
param.help: Single merged prediction file whose extra dimensions should be transferred to originals.

param.name: merged_file_is_copc
param.label: Merged file is COPC LAZ
param.help: Preserve the .copc.laz suffix for tools that infer COPC status from the file name.

param.name: collection
param.label: Segmented files collection
param.help: Filtered/merged high-resolution tiles of one model, as produced by the merge task (optionally after DetailView).

param.name: type
param.label: Model
param.help: RayCloudTools collections also need the filtered tree tables from the merge task.
param.option: SegmentAnyTree, ForestMamba or other point predictions

param.name: tree_files
param.label: RayCloudTools tree tables
param.help: The filtered *_trees.txt and *_trees_info.txt tables emitted by the merge task.

param.name: tree_meshes
param.label: RayCloudTools QSM tree meshes
param.help: Optional: the filtered tree meshes emitted by the merge task.

param.label: Dimension allowlist
param.help: Comma-separated extra dimensions to transfer; empty transfers all extra dimensions.

validator.message: Use comma-separated dimension names containing only letters, numbers, and underscores.

param.name: original_files
param.label: Original LAZ/LAS files
param.help: Original uploaded files to enrich with remapped prediction dimensions.

param.name: original_with_predictions
param.label: Original-with-predictions files
param.help: Original files that already contain prediction dimensions.

repeat.name: additional_versions
repeat.title: Further version of the same originals
repeat.help: Add the same original files with the attributes of another segmentation output (for example a second remap run). Files are matched by name and must hold the same points in the same record order; every version's attributes are combined into one product. An attribute in several versions must have equal values.

param.label: Output formats
param.help: Select one or more output encodings for prod-merged products.

collection.name: output_remap_tree_meshes
collection.label: ${tool.name}: RayCloudTools QSM tree meshes per original
collection.filter: operation['task'] == "remap" or (operation['task'] == "merge" and operation['input_original_laz'] and operation['model']['type'] == "raycloudtools")

collection.name: output_remap_tree_files
collection.label: ${tool.name}: RayCloudTools tree tables per original
collection.filter: operation['task'] == "remap" or (operation['task'] == "merge" and operation['input_original_laz'] and operation['model']['type'] == "raycloudtools")

collection.name: prod_merged_outputs
collection.label: ${tool.name}: Prod-merged LAZ/COPC products
collection.filter: (operation['task'] == "create_merged_file" and ("laz" in operation['merged_output_formats'] or "copc.laz" in operation['merged_output_formats'])) or (operation['task'] == "remap" and operation['prod_merged']['create'] == "True" and ("laz" in operation['prod_merged']['merged_output_formats'] or "copc.laz" in operation['prod_merged']['merged_output_formats'])) or (operation['task'] == "merge" and operation['prod_merged']['create'] == "True" and operation['input_original_laz'] and ("laz" in operation['prod_merged']['merged_output_formats'] or "copc.laz" in operation['prod_merged']['merged_output_formats']))

collection.name: prod_merged_ply_outputs
collection.label: ${tool.name}: Prod-merged PLY products
collection.filter: (operation['task'] == "create_merged_file" and "ply" in operation['merged_output_formats']) or (operation['task'] == "remap" and operation['prod_merged']['create'] == "True" and "ply" in operation['prod_merged']['merged_output_formats']) or (operation['task'] == "merge" and operation['prod_merged']['create'] == "True" and operation['input_original_laz'] and "ply" in operation['prod_merged']['merged_output_formats'])

tool.help:
**What it does**
SmartTile splits large point clouds into tiles for the segmentation models and puts their predictions back together: on one consistent set of trees across tile borders, and on every point of the original upload. Each run performs one task; select it at the top of the form.
**How to wire it up**
*A. A segmentation model plus a tool on the high-resolution tiles.* Tile once with a low (for example 10 cm) and a high (for example 1 cm) resolution. Run the model on the low-resolution tiles and its result through Filter/Merge with the high-resolution tiles and the tile bounds JSON. A tool that works on the merged high-resolution tiles (here DetailView) adds its own collection. Remap takes every collection at once (one repeat entry each) plus the originals. For further models, add one model and one Filter/Merge run each.
.. image:: $PATH_TO_IMAGES/smarttile_workflow_a.png :alt: Workflow A: Tile, SegmentAnyTree, Filter/Merge, DetailView and Remap :width: 1458px :class: img-fluid
*B. One model, shortcut.* Give Filter/Merge the original files as well: it then enriches them with the same code as Remap (100% coverage check included) and returns them as "Original files with predictions" (plus the RayCloudTools tables and meshes per original), and writes the prod-merged products if selected.
.. image:: $PATH_TO_IMAGES/smarttile_workflow_b.png :alt: Workflow B: Tile, SegmentAnyTree and Filter/Merge with originals :width: 970px :class: img-fluid
*C. A per-point tool, no instances.* A tool that only adds a per-point value (for example a classification) on the high-resolution tiles, and keeps every point, needs no Filter/Merge: remap its output directly.
.. image:: $PATH_TO_IMAGES/smarttile_workflow_c.png :alt: Workflow C: Tile, a per-point tool and Remap :width: 970px :class: img-fluid
*D. Combine files into one product.* Create prod-merged file merges several LAZ/LAS files (originals with predictions, or plain uploads) into one download product per resolution.
.. image:: $PATH_TO_IMAGES/smarttile_workflow_d.png :alt: Workflow D: Create prod-merged file :width: 482px :class: img-fluid
-----
**Tile and subsample**
Splits one or more LAZ/LAS point clouds into buffered spatial tiles and writes one subsampled collection per "Subsampled output" entry (default: one 10 cm LAZ output). The tile task also writes a tiling preview image and a tile bounds JSON file. Use the tile bounds JSON with the merge task so SmartTile can identify tile cores and buffers consistently.
All inputs must share one projected CRS in metres (for example UTM), or all carry no CRS (local metres). Tile length, buffer and resolutions are metric distances, so the tile task stops with a CRS error for geographic (degree, e.g. EPSG:4326), geocentric (e.g. EPSG:4978) or foot-based CRSs, for inputs with different CRSs, and for a mix of files with and without a CRS. Reproject such data before upload.
With center of mass (the default), every output point is the exact mean of the original points in its voxel; with nearest to centroid, it is the original point closest to that mean. Both work at every resolution, and the inputs are read only once for all outputs. Add an entry per resolution you need (1 to 100 cm, each resolution once); each can be LAZ, COPC LAZ (only for viewers or spatial reads; COPC conversion is the largest remaining cost on very large datasets) or binary PLY (CRS as a ``comment crs:`` line). Typically a low resolution (10 cm) feeds the segmentation models and a high resolution (1 cm) is the merge geometry; the merge task accepts LAZ and COPC LAZ.
The job needs scratch disk in its working directory: roughly 16 bytes per input point plus 20 bytes per output point (a 3.7-billion-point dataset spilled 56 GiB).
**Filter/Merge segmented tiles**
Transfers each tile's predictions onto its high-resolution geometry, then removes whole instances whose ownership anchor lies outside the tile core toward a neighboring tile. Remaining overlap duplicates are removed only when a surviving point with agreeing labels lies within 1 cm. The merged tiles have distinct instances: every instance ID is in exactly one tile, so DetailView and other per-tile tools see each tree once and whole (a tree that two tiles segmented differently moves whole into the tile whose core holds its centre; no point is dropped). Output tiles keep their tile names (for example ``c00_r00``). Provide the segmented prediction files, the high-resolution tiles, and the tile bounds JSON from the same tiling run. The job's working directory keeps a merge report of every ownership, recovery and deduplication decision and a per-instance summary as local evidence; they are not Galaxy outputs.
For RayCloudTools predictions (``PredInstance_RCT``), supply both tree tables per tile. SmartTile keeps whole trees, never moves points between trees and does not reconcile IDs across tiles. Retained IDs are written as ``tile_id * 100000 + local_id`` in the tiles and in both filtered tables; small-cluster reassignment is not available for them.
Optional small-cluster reassignment runs after deduplication on the final high-resolution tiles: an instance with fewer than the maximum cluster size (default 3,000 points) and a bounding box below the maximum volume (default 4 m³) takes the ID of the remaining instance with the nearest XY centroid (horizontal distance, height ignored) within 5 m. Only instance IDs change; the summary JSON lists ``reassigned_from`` per instance.
When original LAZ/LAS files are provided, the merge task can also transfer predictions back to the originals and create prod-merged products.
**Remap predictions to originals**
Transfers prediction dimensions from either one merged prediction file or one or more segmented prediction collections back onto the original uploaded LAZ/LAS files. Every original point must lie within the matching radius (the voxel diagonal of the high-resolution tiles, 17.32 mm at 1 cm) of a final prediction point: every non-RCT model must cover 100% of the original points. Merge already checked the tiles themselves, so remap needs neither the high-resolution tiles nor a merge manifest. RCT points without a surviving tree within the radius become background ``0``; the coverage report in the job's working directory counts them (local evidence, not a Galaxy output).
RCT tree IDs are compacted once across the dataset to ``1..N``. Each original ``NAME.laz`` gets matching ``NAME_trees.txt`` and ``NAME_trees_info.txt`` tables. Choose RayCloudTools as the model type of the RCT prediction collection and add the filtered tree tables from the merge task.
Optional QSM tree meshes (RayCloudTools 1.3.0+ ``*_trees_mesh.ply``, per-face ``tree_id``) follow the same IDs: merge keeps only the faces of retained trees with tile-prefixed IDs; remap writes ``NAME_trees_mesh.ply`` per original with the complete retained model of exactly the trees in its tables and the final compact IDs. Supply a mesh for every tile or none. Terrain meshes are not processed. Use the dimension allowlist only when you want to copy a selected set of prediction dimensions from segmented collections.
**Create prod-merged file**
Creates delivery-ready products from original-with-prediction files, or from any set of LAZ/LAS files to combine into one product. Instance IDs must already be distinct across all input files: the files are combined as they are, and IDs are never renumbered (originals with predictions from Filter/Merge or Remap meet this). Subsampled products keep one original point per voxel. Full resolution writes ``merged.laz`` (or ``merged.copc.laz`` / ``merged.ply``) with every input point, file by file in name order and in record order, and by default adds ``OriginalPointIndex`` (uint64, the first ExtraByte): each point's position in that order. ForestStructure uses it to restore the source order after COPC and reproduce Julia's results. Full resolution needs LAS/LAZ inputs with one point format, ExtraBytes and CRS. To combine several segmentation outputs, add each further version of the same originals as a repeat entry: files are matched by name, must hold the same points in the same record order, and every version's attributes end up in the product (an attribute in several versions must have equal values). Prod-merged outputs can be LAZ, COPC LAZ, or binary PLY. COPC LAZ is selected with the format value ``copc.laz`` and is returned to Galaxy as ``laz``; PLY is returned as ``plybinary``.
